summary.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue fell 3.2% YoY to Rs 117 crore, but EBITDA margin rose to 6.9% on better domestic realisations as Chinese dumping eased.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue from operations was Rs 117 crore, down 3.2% YoY, with EBITDA of Rs 8 crore at a 6.9% margin and adjusted PAT of Rs 3.7 crore. Management attributed the margin recovery mainly to better domestic price realisation as Chinese dumping of dimer acid moderated from around February 2026. For FY26, revenue fell 14.5% to Rs 460 crore on volume of 44,000 tonnes versus 54,000 tonnes in FY25. Management guided to 75-80% capacity utilisation on the 80,000-tonne base in FY27 and targets around 8% EBIT margin, with a new 40,000-tonne oleochemical product line planned for commissioning in Q2 FY27.

segments.name: Dimer acid
segments.commentary: Contributed close to Rs 140 crore in FY26, about 25-30% of revenue. Chinese dumping at 800-1,000 tonnes per month has eased.

segments.name: Isosteric acid
segments.commentary: Contributed about Rs 26 crore in FY26, about 5-6% of revenue. US marketing was on hold during the 50% duty period and has restarted; cosmetics approval cycles are long.

segments.name: Linoleic acid
segments.commentary: Management put its share of FY26 revenue at around 30%. Realisations are said to be improving slightly as paint demand recovers.

guidance_outlook: FY27 capacity utilisation target of 75-80% on the 80,000-tonne base, versus about 65-66% now; management expects more than 95% utilisation within two years.
Management expects FY27 EBIT margin of about 8%, which management says should continue, with operating leverage able to lift margins further at higher utilisation.

Export share expected to rise from about 8-10% to around 20%, mainly from US, Europe and Japan; US commercial exports restarted about two months ago on a small scale and meaningful volumes are expected within about six months.
Bypass fat (PFAD-based) plant to start operation next month, with revenue contribution from Q3 FY27 onwards, ramping slowly.

New 40,000-tonne oleochemical product: first-phase capex of Rs 20-25 crore, initial capacity around 8,000 tonnes, commissioning around end of Q2 FY27, with 2-2.5 years for validation and customer approval; management theoretically cites Rs 800-1,000 crore revenue at full scale over about five years.
Working capital expected to stay around 100-120 days; inventory days should improve modestly with higher volumes.
No major capex planned for FY27 apart from energy-saving projects with payback under four years; further capex in FY28 depends on the new product.
capex_capacity: Installed capacity is 80,000 tonnes, operating at about 65-66% utilisation; FY26 volume was 44,000 tonnes against a prior peak of about 63,000 tonnes in FY24.

Energy audit completed; investments in electrical equipment, pumps, motors and heat exchangers have cut power and fuel cost to Rs 6 crore in Q4 FY26 from Rs 8 crore in Q4 FY25. Further reduction is expected, and a second energy audit is under way.
New 40,000-tonne novel-process oleochemical line: lab, pilot and plant stages completed; commissioning around Q2 FY27 with first-phase capex of Rs 20-25 crore.
Bypass fat plant starts next month.
The tocopherol / Vitamin E plant is not being utilised because of weak Vitamin E demand and will restart when demand recovers.
demand_pricing: Paint demand showed a recovery in March 2026 and a stronger recovery in Q4; management says paint sector has been looking up for about two months.
Realisations rose about 8-10% on major products as Chinese dumping eased from around February 2026; management described them as 'fairly good'.
Chinese dumping of dimer acid is said to have been about 800-1,000 tonnes per month; the cause is linked to removal of Chinese export incentives of up to 15%.
Management says sales are spread across inks, paints, polyamides (epoxy hardener) and drilling fluids with no major customer concentration.

Raw material is a buy-sell commodity priced daily from refineries with no long-term contracts; end-product prices with customers are revised at most monthly. Import duty on raw vegetable oil is 16.5%; dimer acid import duty is 7.5%.
Management says the rupee depreciation helps exports more than it raises raw material and coal costs, but no sensitivity figures were given.

qa_highlights.question: Would margins return to FY25 EBIT of about 8%, or expand further?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margins will be better this year and it is confident of reaching 8%; at 95% utilisation margins can creep up, with operating leverage. A later question on 12-15% margins was answered as 'our dream' without a commitment.

qa_highlights.question: What share of FY26 revenue came from dimer acid, isosteric acid and linoleic acid?
qa_highlights.answer: Dimer acid about Rs 140 crore (25-30%), isosteric acid Rs 26 crore (5-6%), linoleic acid around 30%.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 40,000-tonne new product linked to paints or cosmetics, and what revenue and margin can it generate?
qa_highlights.answer: It is an oleochemical-basket product, not paint-related. Management cited Rs 800-1,000 crore at full scale over about five years and margins 'much better' than the traditional business, with the analyst's 15-18% range not disputed.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the expansion delayed?
qa_highlights.answer: Raw material duties rose from 5.5% to as high as 27.5% and Chinese dumping hit finished products, so the company avoided debt-funded expansion until conditions stabilised.

qa_highlights.question: Can Chinese dumping restart at current prices?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Chinese incentives could be reinstated but it did not expect that, and at current prices the company is 'happy'.

qa_highlights.question: What are FY27 export expectations and geographies?
qa_highlights.answer: Exports are about 8-10% now, expected to reach about 20%, focused on US, Europe and Japan; US commercial exports started about two months ago.

risks_watch: Sustainability of the Chinese dumping relief; management acknowledged Chinese incentives could be reinstated.
Timeline of the new 40,000-tonne product: 2-2.5 years for validation, and revenue ramp-up expected only over about five years.
Isosteric acid ramp-up in cosmetics faces long approval cycles of 6-8 months for samples and a further 6-8 months after the first commercial shipment.
Raw material cost pass-through: vegetable oil and raw material costs rise with rupee depreciation, and both raw materials and end-product prices reset monthly or daily.
Working capital at 100-120 days with inventory days rising to about 90-95 days.
Dividend cut to Rs 1 per share from Rs 7.5, attributed by management to temporary earnings loss.
summary.management_tone: Cautiously optimistic: management stated confidence on margin recovery and utilisation, but gave few numbers on pricing and deferred several answers (per-kg realisation, FX sensitivity). Long-term targets such as Rs 2,000 crore revenue and 12-15% margins were described as aspirational.
key_quotes: Yes, we have start seen recovery during the month of March and even during this quarter, we see a robust recovery happening.
Margins are going to be better this year. I mean, obviously, we are targeting to reach 8% margins.
Yes, that is our dream. Obviously, we will work hard to achieve that. We will try our best.
It is basically a five-year thing.
